statements.name: doNothing
statements.description: Do nothing -- use this as a placeholder, e.g. in an `if` branch.

statements.name: flush
statements.description: Settle everything that follows spell state NOW:  pending derived checks, then the host's Solid.

statements.name: checkProp
statements.description: Warn if `value` fails `check` for `property`.

statements.name: newThingLike
statements.description: Create an new, "empty" instance of `thing.constructor`.

statements.name: newScratch
statements.description: New SCRATCH `constructor`, e.g. `map()`'s result, or `a copy of the pile as a pile`:
Maps a JS `typeof`/constructor-name result to the `spell`-facing type name shown to users.

statements.name: typeOf
statements.description: Return string "type" of `thing`, as shown to `spell` users:
Special methods for `isOfType()`, for type names `typeOf()` never actually returns (`integer`, `character`, `char`) -- checked instead of a plain `=== typeOf(thing)` comparison.

statements.name: typesOf
statements.description: Types `thing` is, most specific first:  its `typeOf()`, then each super-class's.

statements.name: isOfType
statements.description: Is `thing` an instance of string `type`, or of a sub-type of it -- as per `spellCore.typesOf()`?

statements.name: matchesType
statements.description: Is `thing` of `otherThing`'s type -- the same type, or a sub-type of it?

statements.name: isANumber
statements.description: Is `thing` a valid number (doesn't include NaN).

statements.name: isAnInteger
statements.description: Is `thing` a valid integer (doesn't include NaN). NOTE: treats `0` as an integer as well. ???

statements.name: isArrayLike
statements.description: Is `thing` an array-like thing (`Array`, `arguments`, or anything with a numeric `length`)?

statements.name: isTruthy
statements.description: Assert that `value` is not `false`, `null` or `undefined`. NOTE: explicitly does NOT include `0` -- unlike plain JS truthiness, `0` counts as truthy here.

statements.name: isDefined
statements.description: Return `true` if `value` is defined (e.g. not `undefined`).

statements.name: get
statements.description: Get `path` off `thing`. TODO: unimplemented stub -- always returns `undefined`, no caller wires this up yet.

statements.name: set
statements.description: Set `path` on `thing` to `value`. TODO: unimplemented stub -- currently a no-op, no caller wires this up yet.

statements.name: equals
statements.description: Does `thing` conceptually equal `otherThing`?  Uses lodash `isEqual` semantics (deep, structural).

statements.name: absoluteValue
statements.description: `number` without its sign:  `-3` => `3`.

statements.name: seedRandom
statements.description: Start the random numbers again from `seed`:  everything random after it repeats, run after run.

statements.name: random
statements.description: The next random number:  at least 0 and less than 1 -- the core's own `Math.random()`.

statements.name: randomNumber
statements.description: Random whole number from `min` to `max`, BOTH included.

statements.name: shuffled
statements.description: A new array of `items`, in a random order:  `items` itself doesn't change.

statements.name: countTo
statements.description: `[1, 2, ... count]`:  one number per time round a `repeat {count} times` loop -- `[]` if `count` is under 1.

statements.name: getRange
statements.description: Return a range of numbers from `start` to `end`, inclusive -- counts down if `start > end`.

statements.name: repeat
statements.description: Call `callback()` `count` times, ignoring its return value. TODO: `repeat {number} times` currently compiles to `spellCore.map(spellCore.getRange(...), ...)` instead (see `rules/lists/RepeatNTimes.ts`) -- no rule currently calls this method; confirm whether it's still needed.

statements.name: itemCountOf
statements.description: Number of items in `collection`.

statements.name: isEmpty
statements.description: Is `collection` empty?

statements.name: keysOf
statements.description: Return proper `Array` of "keys" of `collection`.

statements.name: valuesOf
statements.description: Return proper `Array` of values of `collection`.

statements.name: positionOf
statements.description: Position of the first `thing` in `collection` -- see `positionOf()`, below, which it is.

statements.name: getItemAt
statements.description: The item at `position` of `collection`.

statements.name: setItemAt
statements.description: Set the item at `position` of `collection` to `value`.

statements.name: addAtPosition
statements.description: Add `things` in the middle of the `collection` at index `start`, from 0, moving things from `start` on down. Array only.

statements.name: removeItemAt
statements.description: Remove the item at `position` of `collection`.

statements.name: clear
statements.description: Remove all things from the `collection`, in-place.

statements.name: getIteratorFor
statements.description: Return an invoked iterator which yields `[value, position, collection]` for each item in the collection.

statements.name: includes
statements.description: Does `collection` include ALL of the specified `values`?

statements.name: includesAny
statements.description: Does `collection` include any of the specified `values`?

statements.name: duplicateList
statements.description: Return a duplicate of the list.

statements.name: mergeListsInto
statements.description: Merge all `source` list(s) into `destination`, in place.

statements.name: mergeLists
statements.description: Given a list of lists, merge into a new one of the same type as the first in the list.

statements.name: startsWith
statements.description: Is `thing` the first thing in `collection`?  Array only.

statements.name: endsWith
statements.description: Is `thing` the last thing in `collection`?  Array only.

statements.name: prepend
statements.description: Add `things` to front of `collection`, pushing everything else down.  Array only.

statements.name: append
statements.description: Add `things` to end of `collection`.  Array only.

statements.name: addBefore
statements.description: Add `things` just before `item` in `collection`, pushing `item` and what follows down.  Array only.

statements.name: addAfter
statements.description: Add `things` just after `item` in `collection`, pushing what follows it down.  Array only.

statements.name: setItemsOf
statements.description: Set the items from index `start` on to `values`, in turn.

statements.name: reverse
statements.description: Reverse list in-place.  Array only.

statements.name: rangeBetween
statements.description: The items of `collection` from index `start` up to, not including, `end`:  `slice()`'s range.

statements.name: removeRangeBetween
statements.description: Remove the items of `collection` from index `start` up to, not including, `end`, as `rangeBetween()` reads them.

statements.name: rangeStartingAt
statements.description: `count` items of `collection` from index `start` on.  Array only.

statements.name: forEach
statements.description: Execute `method` for each item in `collection`, ignoring results.

statements.name: forEachSequential
statements.description: Execute `method` for each item of map, `await`ing method's completion.

statements.name: map
statements.description: Execute `method` for each item in `collection`, returning results in same type as `collection`.

statements.name: filter
statements.description: Return new `collection` of only things which match `condition` filter.

statements.name: all
statements.description: Return `true` if all items in collection match `condition`, called as `condition(value, position, collection)`.

statements.name: any
statements.description: Return `true` if at least one item in collection matches `condition`, called as `condition(value, position, collection)`.

statements.name: removeItemsAt
statements.description: Remove the items at `positions` of `collection`.

statements.name: remove
statements.description: Remove all occurrences of `things` from collection, in-place.

statements.name: removeWhere
statements.description: Remove items from `collection` which match `condition`, called as `condition(value, position, collection)`.

statements.name: move
statements.description: Move `thing` to `collection` -- `move the card to the tableau`: if the list holding it lets it go, and `collection` takes it.

statements.name: canTake
statements.description: Would `collection` take `thing`, moved there?

statements.name: canGiveUp
statements.description: Would `collection` give up `thing`, moved elsewhere?

statements.name: randomItemOf
statements.description: Return a single item from `collection`, picked randomly.

statements.name: randomItemsOf
statements.description: Return list of up to `count` items from `collection`, picked randomly, each item at most once.

statements.name: randomize
statements.description: Randomize `collection` in-place.

statements.name: smallestOf
statements.description: Return smallest item of `collection` according to `<` comparison.

statements.name: largestOf
statements.description: Return largest item of `collection` according to `>` comparison.

statements.name: doubleQuote
statements.description: Wrap `thing` in double quotes -- no-op if `thing` is already a double-quoted string.

statements.name: backTickQuote
statements.description: Wrap `thing` in back-ticks -- no-op if `thing` is already a back-ticked string.

statements.name: upperCase
statements.description: Stringify and convert to UPPERCASE.

statements.name: lowerCase
statements.description: Stringify and convert to lowercase.
Multiplier from a unit name to milliseconds, e.g. `spellCore.TIME_UNITS_MAP.tick`.

statements.name: pauseFor
statements.description: Return promise which resolves after `number` `units` have elapsed.

statements.name: notify
statements.description: Show `message` for a moment, in a toast -- compiled from `notify "Saved!"`.

statements.name: alert
statements.description: Show `message` in a dialog, and wait until it's closed -- compiled from `alert "Yo!"` (`await`ed).

statements.name: confirm
statements.description: Ask a yes / no question in a dialog:  `true` for ok -- compiled from `confirm "Delete?"` (`await`ed).

statements.name: prompt
statements.description: Ask for some text in a dialog:  what was typed, or `undefined` if cancelled.

statements.name: installStyles
statements.description: Create/initialize a `name`d stylesheet with specified `css` text.

statements.name: drawThing
statements.description: `drawable` drawn -- `null` if it can't draw (no `draw()`).

statements.name: drawOwn
statements.description: `drawable`'s OWN drawing, in its own error boundary, never its element -- `null` if it can't draw (no `draw()`).

statements.name: drawItems
statements.description: Each item of `list`, drawn in its own error boundary -- `null` if `list` has no items to draw.

statements.name: mountApp
statements.description: Mount `app`'s drawing into `element` -- replacing what was there -- and return how to take it down again.
How the page defines the element for a drawable class -- `undefined` until the page running programs sets it.

statements.name: defineElement
statements.description: Name the element of drawable class `Class`, in project `project`, e.g. `<solitaire-card>` -- its tag.

statements.name: useElement
statements.description: Hand the page `ElementClass`, the element class compiled TypeScript writes for drawable class `Class` (epic `drawable-thing` P10, J41): `spellCore.useElement(Card, CardElement)`, right after `class CardElement extends SpellElement<Card>`.

statements.name: elementClassOf
statements.description: The element class handed for drawable class `Class` (`useElement()`) -- `undefined` if none was.

statements.name: elementFor
statements.description: Tag of `drawable`'s element, defined on the page.

statements.name: elementApiOf
statements.description: What drawable class `Class` shows on the outside of its element (epic `drawable-thing` P8):

statements.name: thingFor
statements.description: The program's thing of class `Class` that a tag's `id` names, e.g. the tableau named `T1` for `<solitaire-tableau id="T1">` (epic `drawable-thing` P9, J43).

statements.name: elementTagOf
statements.description: Tag of `drawable`'s element, e.g. `solitaire-card` -- `undefined` if its class has none.

statements.name: thingForReference
statements.description: The program's thing `reference` names, e.g. the tableau named T1 for `Tableau#T1` -- `undefined` if none.

statements.name: thingCalled
statements.description: The program's thing of class `Class` that `text` names, as the part of a reference after its `#` -- `undefined` if none:

statements.name: thingNamed
statements.description: The program's thing of class `Class`, or of a sub-class, named `name` -- `undefined` if none.

statements.name: thingAtPlace
statements.description: The program's thing of class `Class` at place `place`, in the order it made them, counting from 1 -- `undefined` if there's none there.

statements.name: referenceFor
statements.description: The reference that finds `thing` again, e.g. `Tableau#T1` -- `undefined` if no reference does.

statements.name: elementIdFor
statements.description: The `id` an element the program draws for `thing` takes:  its name, e.g. `queen-of-spades` (J43) -- `undefined` for a thing with no name.

statements.name: getPath
statements.description: Given an `object` and a string `path`, walk it to get the leaf value -- see `getPath()` in `$/util`.

statements.name: setPath
statements.description: Given an `object`, walk `path` and set leaf step to `value` -- see `setPath()` in `$/util`.

statements.name: splitPath
statements.description: Split `path` into an array of steps, e.g. `["a", "b", 0, "c"]` -- see `splitPath()` in `$/util`.
Currently-running dynamic test, if any.

statements.name: test
statements.description: Dynamic test: prints to console for now...

statements.name: startTest
statements.description: Begin a named test run, becoming `spellCore.ACTIVE_TEST`.

statements.name: echo
statements.description: Print `message`, grouped under current test if one's running.

statements.name: echoTestAction
statements.description: Print `▶️ Executing` plus back-tick-quoted `message`, grouped under current test if one's running.

statements.name: endTest
statements.description: End currently-running test (if any), logging its icon-prefixed `message` as a console group containing all buffered `output`.

statements.name: expect
statements.description: Return message as to whether a runtime assertion is true or false.
The shared `SpellConsole` instance, exposed as `spellCore.console`.
Set to `true` to show debug messages for `spellCore.RUNTIME` actions.
Set to `true` to show debug messages for process start/stop actions.

statements.name: on
statements.section: Events -- the running program's, on RUNTIME
statements.description: `spellCore.on(...)`:  compiled JavaScript's spelling of `on()` -- see `on()`.

statements.name: off
statements.section: Events -- the running program's, on RUNTIME
statements.description: `spellCore.off(...)` -- see `off()`.

statements.name: once
statements.section: Events -- the running program's, on RUNTIME
statements.description: `spellCore.once(...)` -- see `once()`.

statements.name: trigger
statements.section: Events -- the running program's, on RUNTIME
statements.description: `spellCore.trigger(...)` -- see `trigger()`.
Global runtime state root.

statements.name: resetRuntime
statements.description: Reset `spellCore.RUNTIME`, e.g. when a project starts or a test is run. Returns the new runtime.

statements.name: clearRuntime
statements.description: Clear `spellCore.RUNTIME`:  unset again, as before the first `resetRuntime()` -- see `RUNTIME`.

statements.name: getRuntimeState
statements.description: Return `name`d section of state in our `RUNTIME` environment:

statements.name: clearRuntimeState
statements.description: Reset (clear) `name`d state in our `RUNTIME`. Warns if RUNTIME is not set up.

statements.name: getProcessFlags
statements.description: Initialize and return process flags for the current `spellCore.RUNTIME`. If `RUNTIME` is not set up, warns and returns a new object each time.

statements.name: startProcess
statements.description: Start a conceptual process by `name`.

statements.name: processIsRunning
statements.description: Is a given process running?

statements.name: stopProcess
statements.description: Stop a given process.
Each still alive, in the order they were made.

statements.name: heading
statements.description: The program's running the code under heading `text` now, e.g. `set up all piles` for `## set up all piles`: what it makes from here on was made under it.

statements.name: fromJSON
statements.description: `json` read back as what it was:  each object with a `"@type"` rebuilt as the program's class of that name, each of its props rebuilt the same way, and so on down.
Is a recompiled program loading, to take over the last run's things?

statements.name: carryOver
statements.description: Put the last run's things in place of the new run's -- see the file's header.

statements.name: carryProblems
statements.description: Why each of the last run's things that `carryOver()` would start afresh can't come over -- `[]` if they all can.
Base types known to the `spell` language/parser -- see `SPELL_BASE_TYPES`.
Is the app's page laid out in markup, around the program?  Then `App.start()` draws nothing: the markup is the app's drawing, and its tags find their things (epic `drawable-thing` P9).
DOM `id` of the element an `App` mounts into when the host set no `appRoot`.
Element `App.start()` mounts into, if the host says -- e.g. `<spell-app>`'s, inside its shadow root.

statements.name: appElement
statements.description: Element the app mounts into:  `appRoot`, else `#spell-app-root` in `document` -- `null` if neither.

statements.name: domRoot
statements.description: Document or shadow root the app lives in:  `appRoot`'s shadow root, if it's in one, else `document`.
`Thing`: base for all object-like things in spell -- what `a task is a thing` extends. All things can be drawn, with Solid (`drawing.ts`), e.g.:
`List`: our array concept -- what `a deck is a list` extends.
`App`: a `Thing` that draws a whole application -- what `a game is an app` extends.
`Drawable`:  a `Thing` drawn as its own custom element -- what `a card is a drawable thing` extends.
`DrawableList`:  a `List` drawn as its own custom element, its items inside it -- what `a pile is a drawable list of cards` extends.

statements.name: h
statements.description: Solid's own `h()`, what compiled JavaScript draws with:  `import { h } from "@spell/core"`.

statements.name: css
statements.description: A drawable type's style sheet, as TEXT:  what its `<css>` block compiles to (epic `drawable-thing`, P10, J14).

statements.description: Position of the first `thing` in `collection` -- see `positionOf()`, below, which it is.
